title: Over 200 ASEAN protesters ordered released from Camp Bagong Diwa
summary: More than 200 protesters have been ordered released by the Muntinlupa City Prosecutor's Office following their arrest during a protest caravan amid the opening of the 49th Association of Southeast…

blocks.text: Supporters and advocacy groups gather outside Camp Bagong Diwa in Taguig City to decry the detention of over 200 ASEAN protesters on Wednesday, November 18, 2026. GMA News image

More than 200 protesters have been ordered released by the Muntinlupa City Prosecutor's Office following their arrest during a protest caravan amid the opening of the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit and Related Summits in Pasay City.
According to a report Wednesday on GMA News' What We Know So Far, the Muntinlupa prosecutor's office issued the release order following the protesters' detention for the past three days.

The marchers have been held at Camp Bagong Diwa in Taguig City after they were apprehended on Sunday, November 15, during a protest action slamming the planned US-led Pax Silica initiative and the presence of US President Donald Trump in the Philippines for the ASEAN Summit.
Activists and various sectoral groups have sounded the alarm over the potential risks of the Pax Silica project on the environment, as well as on the indigenous people it may displace.
The Commission on Human Rights (CHR) has already decried the mass detainment, noting that there were reports of minors being among those apprehended. Some protesters were also noticeably wounded.
The CHR also said that its lawyers and investigators were also initially denied access to the Muntinluipa protestors at Camp Bagong Diwa. — VDV, GMA News
